Mikkel Niklas Frandsen is a medical doctor who serves as a member of the [[styregruppen|Styregruppen]] (Steering Group) for the Acute Surgery Database (Akut Kirurgi Databasen) [^src1]. He represents the Danish Surgical Society (Dansk Kirurgisk Selskab) and Zealand University Hospital Køge (Sjællands Universitetshospital Køge) within Region Zealand (Region Sjælland) [^src1]. Through this role, he contributes to the regional clinical governance and organizational oversight of acute surgery in Denmark [^src1].

The available documentation provides a single mention of Frandsen, listing his professional affiliations and committee membership without detailing specific individual claims, actions, or a personal timeline. His significance in the corpus is tied to his position on the steering group, which is responsible for addressing systemic barriers in quality measurement, managing registration challenges, and guiding the interpretation of clinical indicators for acute high-risk patients across Danish hospitals [^src1].
